title: 15 Best RFP Software in 2026: Features, Prices and Reviews
summary: We tested 15 RFP software tools on AI accuracy, response quality, and ease of use. Find the right fit for your team before you shortlist.
body_markdown:
[RFP](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/what-is-a-request-for-proposal-rfp) software helps companies respond to proposals faster and more accurately. Instead of searching old documents, copying answers from previous submissions, and chasing subject-matter experts, the software organizes your knowledge, generates[AI-drafted responses,](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/blog-posts-ai-in-the-rfp-process-2025) and manages the review process in one place.


The most common pain points are accuracy and coordination. Responses go out with outdated product information because no one caught the change in time. Reviews get delayed because RFPs arrive with tight deadlines and SMEs have full calendars.


The better platforms today handle the full response process with AI, so your team focuses on reviewing and refining rather than writing from scratch.


This guide ranks 15 RFP software platforms on AI quality, automation depth, workflow design, and deployment speed so you can find the right fit for your team.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Inventive AI:** Best for proposal and sales teams that want a fully automated, AI-agentic RFP response system with end-to-end agents, zero hallucination controls, and responses that reflect the actual deal context.
- **AutoRFP:** Best for mid-to-large B2B SaaS teams that need fast AI-generated drafts, automatic Go/No-Go screening, and a library that builds itself over time.
- **Tribble:** Best for distributed teams that want quick setup, Slack-native collaboration, and AI drafting that gets smarter with every edit.
- **1up:** Best for sales and pre-sales teams that need instant, trusted answers to questionnaires directly inside Slack, Salesforce, or a browser.
- **AutogenAI:** Best for bid writers and government tender teams that need AI built for long-form, compliance-heavy proposals, not just short Q&A responses.
- **The remaining tools** : Loopio, Responsive, Conveyor, Qvidian, HeyIris, QorusDocs, RocketDocs, Expedience, DeepRFP, and Arphie, serve teams with more specific needs: enterprise content libraries with deep SME workflows, security questionnaire automation, Microsoft-native environments, financial services compliance, or small-team budgets. Each earns its place depending on your stack, content maturity, and team size.

## **How AI Has Changed the Way RFP Responses Get Done**


‍


Before[AI RFP software](https://www.inventive.ai/) , responding to an RFP was a coordination problem. Questions went to SMEs over email, came back inconsistent and late, and a proposal manager manually reconciled, formatted, and chased the deadline. A 50-question RFP absorbed 2-3 weeks and a dozen people.


**First-generation platforms** solved the coordination layer by introducing:


- Q&A libraries to store and reuse approved answers
- Project workflows to assign questions to the right owners
- Deadline tracking, co-editing, and version control


**That model sped things up but created its own overhead:**


- The Q&A library needed someone to build it, maintain it, and retire stale answers
- Responses still had to be drafted and tailored to each buyer
- Compliance checking was manual
- Competitive positioning was an afterthought


The **current generation of**[AI-agentic platforms](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/why-ai-native-rfp-software-is-replacing-legacy-tools-like-responsive-and-loopio) addresses all of it. The AI connects directly to your existing content (product docs, security policies, past proposals, CRM records) and generates a cited draft for each question with no Q&A library to maintain. Turnaround drops from days to minutes.


The bigger shift is in workflow intelligence.[Autonomous agents](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/scale-your-rfp-rfi-response-with-automation-and-ai) now handle what used to require cross-functional coordination:


- One maps every requirement in the RFP
- A second drafts responses grounded in the specific buyer context, so answers read as written for that deal instead of recycled from the last one
- A third runs a compliance pass, catching gaps and contradictions before submission


Content governance runs underneath all three. Knowledge syncs automatically as source documents update, so when a certification renews or a policy changes, every draft from that point on reflects it instead of pulling from a stale version sitting in an outdated library.


Your team should be reviewing a response, not writing one. They check the draft, fix what's off, and step in only where the AI flagged a gap. Every tool on this list is ranked by how fast and accurately it generates a first draft, and how much of your response process it handles end to end.

## **1. Inventive AI**


[Inventive AI](https://www.inventive.ai/) automates the full RFP response workflow, from document intake to final compliant draft, without a curated answer library. When an RFP comes in, the platform parses it automatically across any format, identifies every question and requirement, maps them to sections, and organizes the project with no manual input. Your team spends time reviewing, not assembling.


The founding team comes from Google AI, Stanford, and UC Berkeley, and has been building LLM and agentic systems since before most RFP tools had AI at all.


### **What the automation covers**


Inventive AI generates a complete first draft of an RFP response in minutes. A 20-step AI pipeline runs across five specialized models, two fine-tuned internally, pulling each response fresh from your connected knowledge sources. Every sentence carries an inline citation, so reviewers trace any answer back to its exact source document in seconds.


For **Excel-based questionnaires,** Inventive fills responses row by row. For **narrative-style proposals** , it generates coherent long-form prose, same pipeline, same source accuracy, same citations throughout.


### **Integrations and content governance**


Inventive connects to[SharePoint](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/sharepoint-rfp-automation) ,[Google Drive](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/google-drive-rfp-automation) ,[Confluence](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/confluence-rfp-automation) ,[Salesforce](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/salesforce-rfp-automation) ,[Notion,](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/notion-rfp-automation)[Zendesk](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/zendesk-rfp-automation) ,[and more](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations) , and keeps them live. Source document updates sync automatically, so the AI always draws from your most current content. Teams using Inventive report responses that are[2x more accurate](https://www.inventive.ai/case-studies/inventive-ai-2x-more-accurate-responses-than-other-rfp-ai-tools-barely-needing-a-tweak) than other RFP AI tools, with RAD AI crediting the live source connections as the key reason.


Teams control which sources feed which sections, compliance docs for security questions, sales materials for commercial ones. Every response logs the exact document version it drew from, giving reviewers and auditors a clear source trail with no Q&A library to build or maintain.

### ‍ **The AI agents working on each response**


- **AI Context Engine (proprietary)** : Before generating any response, Inventive AI pulls context from floated RFP documents, meeting notes, relevant web information, and connected sources. The Iteration Agent then lets you refine any response conversationally, adjust tone, add detail, or reframe for the specific buyer.
- **AI Agents for Strategic Advantage** : The agent shows how a competitor vendor would likely respond to the same questions, giving your team a clear angle to sharpen positioning before submission. The platform also includes agents for customer research, brainstorming, and general web research.
- **Analyzer Agent** : Runs a compliance pass on the finished draft. Checks that every RFP requirement has been addressed, flags contradictions between sections, and reviews tone consistency before anything goes out.


### **How contextual accuracy is maintained**


Inventive's proprietary **AI Conflict Manager** , the first of its kind in this market, actively monitors for conflicts across your connected sources. When a pricing page and a sales deck give different answers to the same question, the platform flags it inline before any response goes out.


When source material doesn't have enough information to generate a confident answer, Inventive AI returns an empty field and signals the gap. Your reviewers see exactly where human input is needed, no fabricated answers make it into the draft.


### **Ease of use and setup**


Inventive AI holds the[#1 spot on G2 for easiest-to-use interface](https://www.g2.com/products/inventive-ai/reviews#product-header) in the RFP software category. The platform is purpose-built for[proposal workflows,](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/define-proposal-writing) project setup, question assignment, bulk review, and export all follow the way proposal teams naturally work. Most new users complete their first project within a day of onboarding.


### **Where it falls short**


The reporting and analytics dashboard is functional but early-stage. Win-rate trend analysis and content gap detection across multiple RFP cycles are on the roadmap, not yet live. Teams that need deep performance dashboards today should factor this into the evaluation.


### **Customer reviews**


*According to*[Gartner](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/product/inventive) *, a verified reviewer from the Media industry said Inventive AI "fundamentally changed how we approach RFP responses by dramatically reducing turnaround time while improving response quality."*

## **2. Loopio**


[Loopio](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/loopio-pricing-features-reviews) is a library-first RFP response platform. It organizes approved Q&A content into a three-tier taxonomy (Stacks, Categories, Subcategories) with freshness scoring and scheduled review cycles to help teams track content currency.


A Browser Extension lets users import RFPs from procurement portals (Ariba, Jaggaer, UpGuard) directly into Loopio, complete responses, and submit back to the portal without leaving the platform. Verified integrations include Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, and Slack.


This is how Loopio scores against the 5 criteria that decide this ranking:


6.0 3.5 8.0 8.5 6.5 5.9


‍


### **Where it shines**


Content governance infrastructure, freshness scoring, review cycles, admin-approval workflows for library updates, and usage analytics. It supports teams with dedicated content managers running high-volume, recurring RFP programs.


### **Limitations**


- Every new certification, product update, or policy change requires someone to update the Q&A library by hand. Skip that step, and the AI can't use it.
- No conflict detection. Contradictory entries in the library are not flagged by the system.
- Loopio isn't AI-native. The platform was built in 2014 as a library-based tool, and AI was bolted on around 2021, not built into the architecture from the start which restricts the AI capabilities in response generation.
- Loopio has no real content governance. Freshness scoring flags how old an entry is, not whether it's correct, and contradictory entries can both look "fresh" with nothing to catch the conflict.


### **Pricing**


Contact for pricing.


### **Customer reviews**


According to[Gartner](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/rfp-response-management-applications/vendor/loopio/product/loopio/review/view/5516656) , a verified reviewer said Loopio helps with RFI responses and saves time through its library, but noted the AI "is not working the way we want," likely because the library isn't sufficiently maintained.


### **Best for**


Enterprise proposal teams with dedicated content managers, mature library programs, and high volumes of recurring RFPs.


***Also Read:***[Loopio vs Inventive AI: A Feature-by-Feature Comparison](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/loopio-vs-inventive-ai)


## **3. Tribble**


[Tribble](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/tribble-ai-review-pricing-features-reviews) is an AI-native platform that builds a knowledge graph from connected content sources Google Drive, Slack, internal wikis and uses it to generate RFP responses. A Chrome extension allows contributors to answer questions directly within Slack or Google Docs without opening a separate application. The reviewer edits feedback into the knowledge graph and influences future response suggestions. Teams typically go live within 2–3 days of connecting their sources.


Here's how Tribble breaks down across the 5 criteria we scored every tool on:

‍


### **Where it shines**


The Chrome extension removes the biggest friction point in distributed RFP collaboration: getting SMEs to contribute on time. Instead of asking subject-matter experts to log into a separate platform, reviewers can answer questions, edit drafts, and approve responses directly within Slack or Google Docs.


### **Limitations**


- Tribble is AI-native, but it still has no real content governance: no conflict detection between sources, and enterprise-grade approval chains and multi-gate review workflows aren't fully built out yet.
- Functionality differs depending on where you're working, the Chrome extension and Slack don't offer identical capabilities, and integration gaps exist with tools like Dynamics 365.
- No deal-specific context engine, so responses don't automatically adjust to the specific buyer.


### **Pricing**


Credit-based pricing. Contact sales for a quote.


### **Customer reviews**


According to[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/tribble/reviews) , **Ray M.** (CEO, Small-Business) said Tribble is very agile and handling both yes/no and long-form responses and easy to train, but wished it integrated with Dynamics 365 Sales.

Mid-market technology companies, distributed teams, and fast-moving organizations where speed of setup and SME collaboration matter more than governance depth.

## **4. Responsive (formerly RFPIO)**


[Responsive](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/responsive-ai-rfpio-pricing-features-reviews) is a library-first enterprise RFP platform. It manages Q&A content through a centralized library and routes responses across teams through configurable workflow steps. The platform includes a TRACE Score (Transparency, Relevance, Accuracy, Completeness, Ethics) that applies a quality validation check to AI-generated responses.


This is how Responsive scores against the 5 criteria that decide this ranking:


6.5 0 7.5 8.5 6.0 5.2


### **Where it shines**


Responsive works well for enterprise teams that manage high volumes of RFPs across multiple departments. Its configurable workflow steps handle cross-functional review and approval across large organizations. The platform's analytics templates give proposal managers visibility into team activity, content usage, and response progress across active projects.


### **Limitations**


- No deal-specific context engine. All responses use the same library-based retrieval regardless of buyer.
- Responsive isn't AI-native. It was built as a library-first response platform, and AI was layered on top of that existing architecture later, so it still runs on the same underlying content library rather than being designed around AI from the start.
- No real content governance. The TRACE Score checks an answer's tone and completeness, not whether it's still accurate or whether two library entries contradict each other.
- Named user licensing means every reviewer,[legal](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/top-ai-tools-legal-rfp-workflow) , IT, product, adds a seat, pushing contract costs well past the base-tier estimate.


### **Pricing**


Quote-based, named user licensing. Lite, Emerging, Growth, and Enterprise tiers. Contact sales.


### **Customer review**


According to[Gartner](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/rfp-response-management-applications/vendor/responsive/product/responsive/review/view/5803884) , a verified reviewer said Responsive is "light in use and easy to navigate after applying filters", but the AI Response section in the Content Library slows page loading and frequently generates wrong product answers.


### **Best for**


Large enterprises with multilingual programs and complex tech ecosystems that need broad workflow integration across multiple business units.

## **9. HeyIris (Iris AI)**


HeyIris is an AI-native response workspace that handles RFPs, RFQs, DDQs, and security questionnaires within one environment. Teams manage intake, AI-assisted drafting, review, and submission without switching between tools. A style control feature lets teams set different tone and response structure standards by questionnaire type. Here's how HeyIris breaks down across the 5 criteria we scored every tool on:


7.0 0 7.0 7.0 6.0 5.2


### **Where it shines**


The AI-assisted drafting layer generates first-pass responses across all questionnaire types, reducing the time contributors spend writing from scratch. Teams can assign sections to specific reviewers, track approval status, and manage deadlines within the same workspace, without coordinating over email or spreadsheets.


### **Limitations**


- No documented content governance. There's nothing in place to catch stale, duplicate, or conflicting answers, so that burden falls back on manual review as the library grows.
- Output quality still depends on how well-maintained your content library is, and reviewers say it struggles with nuanced writing, tone control, and visual or graphical elements.
- G2 review volume is limited, and the strong rating reflects a small early-adopter sample rather than broad enterprise validation.


### **Pricing**


Custom, user-based pricing. Contact sales.


### **Customer review**


According to[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/heyiris-ai-iris/reviews) , **Jeffrey W.** (Validated Reviewer) said HeyIris has been "a force multiplier" for his small RFx team, generating strong first drafts from intent-aware AI and reducing team burnout.


### **Best for**


B2B SaaS teams that need a single platform for multiple inbound questionnaire types with AI-assisted drafting and workflow management.

## **How to Pick the Right RFP Software for Your Team**


Most[RFP software buying decisions](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/top-rfp-software-use) go wrong for the same reason: teams evaluate on demo performance, not on what day-to-day use looks like three months after onboarding. These tips cover what vendors rarely tell you upfront.


### **Run a Live Test With Your Own RFP Before You Commit**


Ask to run a live test using a recent RFP before the sales cycle ends, ideally one you have already submitted, so you can compare the AI's output against what your team actually wrote. Focus specifically on:


- Questions that required SME input or were hard to answer quickly
- Sections where your team had to rewrite or significantly edit previous AI drafts
- Any compliance or security questions with strict language requirements


The gap between the AI's draft and your actual submission tells you exactly how much editing work remains after the platform does its part.


### **Calculate the Revenue Cost of RFPs You Currently Decline**


Most[ROI](https://www.inventive.ai/roi-calculator) conversations with vendors focus on hours saved. A sharper measure is the revenue sitting in RFPs your team passes on entirely.


If your team declined three RFPs last month at $60,000 each, that is $180,000 in pipeline you could not pursue, not because the opportunities were weak, but because there was no bandwidth to respond. Winning back even one of those per month covers the platform cost within a quarter.


Ask vendors: *"Do you have a customer who increased their RFP response volume after onboarding?"* Push for a specific before-and-after number, not a general claim about efficiency.


### **Test the Platform on a Question It Has Never Seen Before**


Before your evaluation ends, ask the AI something your company has genuinely never answered, something completely outside your content library. Example: *"What is the psychological effect of the color blue on purchasing decisions?"*


- A well-built platform says it does not know and flags it for human review
- A poorly built one generates a confident-sounding answer with nothing behind it


Every RFP has questions your team has not seen before. If the platform fabricates answers when it does not know, those answers end up in live submissions, you must check for AI accuracy by doing so.


### **Verify What Each Integration Actually Does**


When a vendor says they integrate with Salesforce or Google Drive, ask one follow-up question: does the platform automatically pull in updates when those documents change, or does it only import content once at setup?


Integration Sync What it means


Live sync Answers stay current as source documents update, no manual effort


One-time import Content goes stale the moment those source documents change


If the answer is a one-time import, move on. Stale content in a live RFP is not an integration, it is a manual maintenance burden you are paying a platform to create.


### **Test Conflict Detection With a Real Scenario**


Pull two internal documents with contradictory information, for example, a product sheet with last year's pricing and a sales deck with the current figure. Feed both into the platform and ask a pricing question.


- **Good behavior:** The platform flags the contradiction and routes it to a human to resolve
- **Red flag:** It picks one answer and moves on without surfacing the conflict


That second scenario means a wrong figure ends up in a submitted RFP with no one catching it.


### **Review Content Governance Controls**


If your team needs legal or compliance sign-off on RFP answers, ask how the platform handles that. Before signing, confirm you can:


- Require approval before a new answer goes live
- Access version history showing who changed what and when
- Restrict editing rights on approved content


Without these controls, an outdated commitment on security or product capability in a submitted RFP becomes your legal team's problem.


### **Check Onboarding Time Before You Sign**


Before committing, read G2 and Gartner reviews specifically for comments on implementation time, real users report how long it took from contract signing to completing their first live RFP, and that number varies significantly:


- **AI-agentic platforms** connected to your existing documents typically go live within days or minutes.
- **Library-first platforms** that require building a content library from scratch can take two to three months.


If you have active RFPs that cannot wait, that timeline difference matters more than any feature comparison.


### **Ask for a Full Pricing Breakdown**


RFP software pricing can get complicated fast. Some platforms charge per user, others cap monthly RFP volume, and some charge extra for integrations you assumed were included. Before signing, get clear answers on:


- What happens if you go over your usage limit
- What adding one more user costs
- Whether all the integrations you need are in the current plan


These are the questions vendors rarely volunteer upfront, and the ones most likely to surface as surprise charges at renewal.

## **FAQs**


**Q1. Will RFP AI generate hallucinated answers that go into live submissions?**


It depends on the platform. Source-grounded tools pull answers from your connected documents and flag gaps instead of filling them, so reviewers see exactly where human input is needed. Generative platforms without source grounding are the risk: they produce confident-sounding answers with nothing behind them. Before buying, test this directly. Ask the AI a question your content library has never addressed. A reliable platform returns an empty field. An unreliable one makes something up.


**Q2. Does RFP software make sense if we only respond to 10–15 RFPs per year?**


Yes. But the value shifts from volume to quality. Low-volume teams often spend disproportionate time on each RFP because there's no repeatable process. An AI-native platform with fast onboarding (days, not months) and per-project pricing means you can be productive from the first submission without a long implementation. If your average deal size is $100K+, one better-quality response that wins is enough to justify the cost.


**Q4. What's the difference between RFP software and proposal tools like PandaDoc or Proposify?**


RFP software is built for inbound procurement, structured questionnaires sent by a buyer with a deadline. Proposal software is built for outbound sales, branded documents your team sends to prospects. The workflows run in opposite directions. RFP tools handle intake, AI drafting, compliance review, and SME coordination. Proposal tools handle design, e-signatures, and deal tracking. Some teams need both, but they solve different problems and shouldn't be evaluated as substitutes.


**Q5. What happens to our company data when we connect internal documents to an AI RFP platform?**


This varies by vendor and is worth confirming before you sign. Ask three questions: Is our data used to train shared AI models? Where is it stored, and under which data residency rules? What happens to our data if we cancel? Vendors with SOC 2 Type 2 certification have been independently audited on data handling. For financial services or healthcare teams with stricter requirements, ask specifically about private AI deployment options where your data never leaves a controlled environment.


**Q6. How do we handle RFP questions we don't have an answer for yet?**


Flag them immediately, don't let them sit until the deadline. Use your platform's SME assignment feature to route those specific questions with context: what's being asked, which section it's in, and when the final review is due. If the information genuinely isn't available before submission, respond with "in progress" language and a committed timeline. Never let the AI fill a knowledge gap with an unverified answer, especially in security or compliance sections.
